title: ASML says it cannot meet chip tool demand in 2027 or 2028
gist: ASML says it cannot meet chip tool demand in 2027 or 2028, with customers asking about 2029-2030 orders, and raised 2026 sales guidance to EUR44-45 billion. The article frames ASML's order book as hard evidence of committed AI investment during a week of chip selloffs and IMF warnings on circular financing.

insights.claim: ASML says its supply plans mean it cannot fully meet demand in 2027 or 2028, and some customers want to place orders for 2029 and 2030.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Multi-year tool backlog signals sustained leading-edge capex commitments.
insights.quote: Customers are asking every single day for more tools, Fouquet said.

insights.claim: ASML in July said it would add 30% more capacity for 2027 and was studying a further 30% for 2028, and CEO Christophe Fouquet now says it is investigating going beyond that.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Capacity expansion is itself capex-intensive and long-lead.

insights.claim: ASML raised the low end of its 2026 sales guidance to between EUR44 billion and EUR45 billion and its shares rose 2.8% to EUR1,551.60.
insights.speaker: L

insights.claim: ASML has completed price conversations with key customers, with the effect visible partly through 2027 and fully from 2028, and China remains about a fifth of this year's revenue.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Pricing power adds to margin upside beyond volume.

insights.claim: A second Dutch ASML campus is under construction with the first phase due in 2029, which is the horizon customers are now asking it to quote for.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: New capacity arrives only in 2029, extending the shortage window.

themes.theme: Order book as evidence versus financial risk

insights.claim: ASML's most advanced tools take more than a year between order and delivery, so its order book records what chipmakers have already committed to rather than what they say, making it the hardest evidence against the AI-bubble argument.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Physical tool orders are stronger demand evidence than sentiment or guidance.
insights.quote: its book is a record of what chipmakers have already committed to rather than what they say

insights.claim: An order for a lithography machine is not a revenue promise but a purchase of a physical object from the only company that makes it.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: ASML's exposure to AI-financing risk is lower than that of circular-financing counterparties.
insights.quote: An order for a lithography machine is not a revenue promise.

insights.claim: The IMF called the sector's circular financing wrong-way risk this week because the investment sours when the promised revenue does.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Financial-stability risk sits in financing structures, not in tool demand.

insights.claim: Chip stocks sold off after Broadcom's chief executive compared investor sentiment to a casino, with Seoul falling 7% intraday, in the same week ASML made its comments.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Sentiment is fragile even as hard orders stay strong.

insights.claim: ASML shares are up 64% this year, making it Europe's most valuable company, but most of the rise came early (about 60% by mid-July) so the stock has been close to flat through the autumn.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: The demand news is largely priced in per the stock's flat autumn.

insights.claim: Europe's best earnings quarter in three years was an energy story, not an AI one, so ASML remains an exception at home.
insights.speaker: L
insights.so_what: Europe has limited broader AI earnings exposure beyond ASML.
